text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian government and depositors have collectively lost 86 billion naira deposited with distressed banks, according to John Ebhodaghe, chief executive of Nigerian Deposit Insurance Company, which underwrites funds placed in banks.
- Warship ordered to move to riot-torn oil-producing area of Warri is yet to arrive because of shallowness of Escravos River through which it has to sail, military sources say.
- Nigerian Railway Corporation has resumed container traffic from Lagos to north central city of Kaduna after break of four years.
- Court adjourns to May 16 ruling on whether or not it has jurisdiction to entertain bail plea by 11 pro-democracy activists charged with treason over bomb explosions.
- Death toll in attack on Koko town in clashes between armed youths over relocation of municipal council headquarters has risen to 20.
- French ambassador in Lagos urges Nigeria to adopt indigenous model of democracy.
